title: Refactor visibility-aware prefetch and implement idempotent redelivery protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current Redis/Kafka worker stack relies on per-consumer prefetch heuristics and an ad-hoc redelivery flow that causes duplicate processing under lease churn and during concurrent restarts. This manifests as: increased tail latency, unexplained duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent handlers, and noisy dashboards from transient redeliveries.

Goal: Replace the brittle per-worker prefetch heuristics with a visibility-aware shared prefetch adapter and introduce a first-class idempotent redelivery protocol that uses stable dedupe keys + a commit-evidence log to prevent duplicated side-effects while preserving low latency. The work also tightens backpressure boundaries so slow consumers cause graceful shedding instead of head-of-line blocking.

Scope:
- Implement a visibility-aware prefetch adapter that coordinates across consumer instances in a shard to keep an in-flight window per-shard (not per-tenant), driven by observed end-to-end latency and KV-cache hit rates.
- Add an idempotent redelivery protocol: generate stable dedupe-id for delivery attempts, persist dedupe evidence in the existing per-tenant metadata store, and expose a lightweight commit-evidence API for workers to mark side-effects completed.
- Strengthen backpressure by coupling prefetch admission to a cooperative shedder that can throttle ingress credits per-shard and surface metrics to Console.
- Provide migration tooling to reconcile in-flight messages during rollout (graceful drain, reassign ownership).
- Add end-to-end integration tests with real Redis & Kafka in the CI harness and a performance validation run on dedicated dev GPUs.

Non-goals: full rewrite of consumer protocol; building a global dedupe store (we will reuse per-tenant metadata with TTL), rewriting downstream services to be idempotent (we will provide commit-evidence to avoid requiring downstream changes).
acceptance_criteria: New visibility-aware prefetch adapter is enabled behind a feature flag and maintains the configured per-shard in-flight window under normal load.
Idempotent redelivery protocol prevents duplicate side-effects for at least 99.9% of simulated restart/redelivery scenarios in the integration test matrix.
End-to-end p99 latency with prefetch enabled does not regress by more than 10% for the standard chat workload compared to baseline.
Console shows new metrics: shard_inflight_window, dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, prefetch_admissions, shedder_throttles.
Migration plan exists and was exercised in a canary (rolling restart) with no lost messages and <0.1% duplicate deliveries measured.
Code reviewed, security checklist completed, and upgrade notes added to Runbook/CONSUMER_UPGRADES.md.

2026-01-30 - Eng review: Raised concern about metadata store write amplification; added batched writes and a lightweight evidence bloom for high-throughput tenants.

2026-02-05 - Marco Chen: Proto impl for prefetch adapter merged to feature branch. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/7829. Notes: added detailed telemetry hooks and feature flag 'prefetch.visibility_shard_v1'.
